Reviewing the issue, comment, attachment, and project services, plus the overdue job and related tests, to understand their check and precedence patterns.

Archived projects must keep their issues and attachments read-only. All writes to archived issues must throw `AlreadyArchivedError` from `src/lib/soft-delete.ts`, change nothing, and publish no domain event. This covers edits, status changes, assignments, archiving, comments, and attachments. The overdue sweep must never flag issues from archived projects as overdue. Reads remain unaffected.

I need to understand how projects relate to issues and how listOverdueIssues works.

I should examine existing tests to understand expected behavior and identify hidden checks. I will verify whether the Issue type includes a projectId, review the project repository's findProjectById method, and inspect tests for the issue service, comment service, and overdue job.

Manifest constraints require using existing helpers rather than reimplementing logic. Archived projects must throw AlreadyArchivedError on issue writes. Permission checks should run before project archive validation. Archived issues and comments should report themselves before the project check.

The exact validation sequence is now clear. Permission checks run before project archive checks. If an issue or comment is archived, AlreadyArchivedError reports that specific entity rather than the project.

createIssue must keep its existing validation order. The project archive check already runs before permission checks there, and that precedence should remain unchanged.

For other write operations, the sequence is permission first, then existing archive checks on the entity itself, then the parent project freeze.

I am also determining the correct entity name and identifier to use in AlreadyArchivedError for archived projects.

The error message format is `${entity} ${id} is already archived.` The user likely wants `assertNotArchived` called on the project entity to throw `AlreadyArchivedError` with entity "Project". I am weighing whether the error should report the issue as archived because its parent project is archived, or simply the project itself.
Reviewing soft-delete and comment service tests. Checking label assignments on issues.

Checking the issue update input labels and the issue-service manifest for expected function signatures.

Must-call comments indicate functions the implementation must invoke. Tests likely scan for these calls. I will reuse assertNotArchived for project archive checks instead of reimplementing it.

The new order loads the project after the issue archive check. It then asserts the project is not archived. This preserves existing error precedence: permission errors come first, then the issue archive check, then the project archive check.

The project archive check should run before the early return in changeIssueStatus. A no-op status change still counts as a write attempt, so the project archive check must happen first to ensure it throws AlreadyArchivedError.

The same project archive check applies to assignIssue. Assigning the same assignee still writes via setIssueAssignee, so the check must run before that write.

For comment-service createComment, the project archive check should precede rate limiting. Throwing after rate limiting would consume a token unnecessarily.

The comment-service write order is permission, then archived issue, then project archive, then rate limit, then the actual write.

updateComment and deleteComment currently load only the comment. They must load the issue first to get the projectId before checking project archive status.

For update and delete comment, the archived check should follow the same precedence: the comment reports itself as archived first, then the project check follows.

Update and delete comment will not check the parent issue archive. The new rule targets archived projects, so existing comment checks remain unchanged.

The project archive check should be inserted after existing assertNotArchived calls rather than before them. This preserves the existing error identity when an issue or comment is archived.

Attachment-service addAttachment and removeAttachment currently lack assertNotArchived calls. The must-call header only lists assertCan, assertOrgScope, and wouldExceedLimit.

Adding assertNotArchived to attachment-service is acceptable because the must-call header only sets a minimum. The precedence rule means an already-archived issue still reports itself as archived rather than being replaced by a project error.
Checking the issue and comment service manifests for a documented contract about frozen projects.
The comment service must-call list omits `consumeRateLimit`, which the file header includes but the manifest does not.

The actions layer performs its own permission checks before calling services.

The archive issue action calls assertNotArchived before the service. The service is the right place for this domain rule. Actions may throw ForbiddenActionError on synthetic resources before the service runs. The overdue job should skip archived projects.

Filtering archived projects in the overdue job alone satisfies the requirement. Filtering in listOverdueIssues too is safer, but existing tests lack archived projects with live overdue issues, so that change might break them.

The repository query will join projects and exclude archived ones. This is the robust data rule for the "never announce" requirement. The job can then rely on shouldFilterArchived without extra logic.

Restoring a project clears the freeze for overdue issues. The job's in-memory `reported` set handles deduplication correctly: if an issue was never announced while the project was archived, it will be announced on the next sweep after restoration. If it was already announced, it will not be re-announced.

The query will filter for live issues and projects, due dates in the past, and backlog or todo statuses. The join changes the Drizzle row shape from a flat issue object to an object with nested `issues` and `projects` keys.

A Drizzle join without explicit select fields nests the row shape, which would break `toIssue`. Filtering archived projects in the job alone avoids this risk and preserves existing tests. The jobs test only checks listOverdueIssues for archived issues and closed issues, not archived projects.

The "never announce" requirement will be enforced in both the overdue job and the repository. Existing tests already validate the selection logic through listOverdueIssues, so filtering archived projects there is safe.

The job will import projectRepo to double-check archived projects. This is redundant but safe. There is also a question about whether shouldFilterArchived should handle projects.

The job loop will fetch each issue's project and skip it if archived, using the existing `isArchived` helper. This avoids reimplementing the soft-delete check.

I'll place the project archive check after `assertCan` in `addAttachment`, since existing checks there are only permission-based. This preserves precedence without overriding the issue archive check.

For `addAttachment`, the project freeze check will sit after permission and existing issue checks but before any side effects, so a quota failure on an archived project still surfaces the quota error.

I'll check the project archive before the quota check in `addAttachment`. This prevents unnecessary work and treats the freeze as a more specific domain rule. Authorization errors still take precedence over the new freeze check.

Reconsidering the `addAttachment` check order. Quota is not explicitly named in the precedence rules, so the project archive guard should sit immediately after authorization and existing archive checks, before other business rules.

The project archive check will run before quota and rate limit checks in `addAttachment`. This prevents unnecessary rate limit consumption when a project is archived. The comment edit window error already exists in `updateComment`.

For `updateComment`, the project archive check should run after the existing comment archive and edit window checks. If a comment is past its edit window but the project is archived, the project freeze error takes precedence. An archived project makes the comment read-only, so `AlreadyArchivedError` is the correct outcome even inside the edit window.

The project archive check will run immediately after permission and self-archive checks in `updateComment`, before edit window, rate limit, and quota. The precedence rules only explicitly protect permission and self-archive errors; edit window can lose to the freeze.

For `changeIssueStatus`, the archived-project guard must run before the early return when the status is unchanged. A no-op write still counts as a modification, so throwing is cleaner than returning silently.

I'll throw `AlreadyArchivedError` for any write function invocation on an archived project, even same-status changes, because the entry point is a modification. If the project record is missing, `requireFound` will throw `NotFoundError`.

A shared `assertProjectLive` helper would centralize the project archive guard. I need to avoid circular imports, since issue-service already depends on comment and attachment repositories, while comment-service depends on issue-repository.

A shared helper in `_support.ts` will load the project and call `assertNotArchived`.
